title: The Extractor Fan (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar spoken word dry wit cabaret 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan male vocal absurdist storytelling warm vinyl late night
lyrics:
[Intro - piano, warm and unhurried]
Now I want to tell you about my uncle
A man of genuine enthusiasms
And his greatest enthusiasm
Was tractors

[Verse 1]
He went to the Royal Show every year
Not for the animals, not for the show bags
Not for the rides or the woodchop or the dagwood dogs
He went for the tractors

He would stand in the pavilion for considerable time
Reading the specifications on the placards
Examining the wheel arch on a John Deere
With the concentration of a man defusing something important

And then one year, something went wrong
A tractor moved
In a direction that did not suit my uncle
And my uncle was in hospital

[Pre-Chorus]
Everyone came to visit
Everyone brought something tractor-themed
A cup, a picture, a poem about tractors
One person brought a small ceramic tractor
Nobody questioned this

[Chorus]
He was the tractor man, he was the tractor man
Everyone knew him by the tractor in his hand
Tractor cup, tractor card, tractor on the shelf
The man and the tractor became one with themselves
He was the tractor man, he was the tractor man
The most committed fan in the land

[Verse 2]
Six months later he was out
His first proper evening, his first night in a room
A woman walked across the floor toward him
Smiling in a way that required attention

She said do you want to get out of here
He said no, I've got this
He breathed in slowly
He breathed out slowly

She looked around
The room had cleared
She said how did you do that
She genuinely wanted to know

[Bridge - spoken, completely level]
He looked at her
He breathed out once more
He said

I am an ex-tractor fan

She considered this
For a reasonable amount of time
She said
We can stay

[Chorus]
He was the tractor man, he was the tractor man
Everyone knew him by the tractor in his hand
Tractor cup, tractor card, tractor on the shelf
The man and the tractor became one with themselves
He was the tractor man, he was the tractor man
The most committed fan in the land

[Outro - piano resolves, warmly]
They stayed for the rest of the evening
He told her about the John Deere specifications
She listened for what she considered an appropriate amount of time
It was a very successful first night out

He still goes to the Royal Show
He stands at a slightly greater distance from the tractors
But the enthusiasm is unchanged
He is, and always will be
An ex-tractor fan
